Build an Ensembl Compara orthology snapshot for your species, and write it as Parquet

proteins_build_orthology.Rd

Build an Ensembl Compara orthology snapshot for a set of species from their gene sets, the gene trees and every species' homology dump, and optionally write it as Parquet and say, gene by gene, how far Compara's inference got in another species.

Answers which mouse genes are orthologous to this human gene, and if none, why not? Wraps mzLib's OrthologySnapshot.Build and OrthologySnapshotWriter.WriteAsync (mzLib #1381): which genes of one species are orthologous to which genes of another, kept exactly as Compara states it. One-to-many and many-to-many orthologies are several rows, paralogs are kept, and nothing is picked, merged or collapsed. Local files only; nothing is downloaded.

Usage

proteins_build_orthology(release, gene_trees, dumps, gtfs = NULL, gene_sets = NULL,
  restrict_gene_trees = FALSE, out = NULL, pair_status = NULL, timeout = NULL)

Arguments

release

The Ensembl release of the Compara inputs, e.g. "116" (a whole number is sent as its digits). Required: mzLib holds the gene trees and every dump to it when their file names carry a release. A GTF's own number is not compared with it (Ensembl publishes some species with their own annotation release).

gene_trees

Compara's gene-tree file, <collection>.GeneTree_content.default.e<release>.txt.gz. It tells a gene whose tree holds no gene of the other species from one whose tree does but got no ortholog call.

dumps

One Compara homology dump per species (homologies/<species>/Compara.<release>.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz), in any order: each dump's species is read from its rows. Sent on stdin after the species lines.

gtfs

A named character vector from species to its Ensembl primary-assembly GTF, plain or .gz: c(homo_sapiens = "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf.gz"). The names are Ensembl production names, as the dumps' species column spells them, and they are the snapshot's species. Sent on stdin, one line per species.

gene_sets

Instead of a GTF, a compact gene table mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter made from one, by species in the same way (it keeps the GTF's provenance, so the snapshot is the same). A species may be in gtfs or gene_sets, not both.

restrict_gene_trees

Keep only the gene-tree members in your gene sets. FALSE (the default) is mzLib's default and keeps every gene in the file - 4.2 million for the vertebrates of release 116. The snapshot is the same either way; only memory differs.

out

A directory to write the snapshot to: Parquet tables (genes/, members/, pairs/), views.sql and manifest.json. It must not exist yet or be empty: mzLib writes a snapshot once and never updates one in place. NULL (the default): nothing is written.

pair_status

c(from_species, to_species): return every gene of from_species with its status in to_species. Two different species of the snapshot, in that order: a status is not symmetric. NULL (the default): not computed.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL (the default) to wait: for human, mouse and rat at release 116, mzLib reports about 20 s to build and 40 s more to write.

Details

Every species' homology dump is required, and mzLib refuses a call without one. Compara puts each of a pair's relationships in one of the pair's two dumps, arbitrarily, and in practice they partition: in release 116 every human-mouse orthology is in the *mouse* dump and none is in the human one. Reading the dump named after your species gives a complete-looking, badly incomplete answer.

Orthology is pairwise and not transitive. A~B and B~C do not make A~C, so never chain pairs into groups. The written views.sql has a species_set3 macro that forms a tuple only when every two members are orthologs.

The relationships are in the Parquet files out writes, which mzLib cannot read back and mzLibR does not read (it has no dependencies): query them with the arrow or duckdb packages, as the proteins article shows. Without out, the call checks that the inputs fit together and, with pair_status, says gene by gene how far Compara's inference got in one other species.

Value

An mzlibr_orthology_snapshot. The relationships themselves are in the Parquet files out writes, not here: this says what went in, what came out, and, with pair_status, every gene's status in one other species.

release is the release you gave; species the snapshot's species, in sorted order; format is "ensembl-orthology-snapshot" and format_version its version, as manifest.json names them. snapshot_id is mzLib's id for the snapshot, a sha256 over the format, the release, the species and every input's sha256: the same inputs give the same id, written or not. Record it with any result drawn from the snapshot. identical_duplicates_dropped counts homology rows found in both of a pair's dumps, identical, and counted once, in rows: 0 in release 116, whose dumps partition.

gene_sets is a data.frame, one row per species: species, source_file_name, sha256 (the value proteins_resolve_genes reports as gene_set_sha256, so a resolution and a snapshot can be checked against one gene set), release, genome_build and genebuild_last_updated (NA when the GTF's name or headers carry none), and gene_count, in genes, every biotype.

gene_trees is a list: source_file_name, sha256, release (NA when the name carries none, so it was not checked), collection (e.g. "vertebrates"), member_count, the genes held from the file, and restricted_to_gene_sets, the gene sets' sha256s the members were restricted to, or NULL when every gene in the file was kept.

dumps is a data.frame, one row per species, the species read from the dump's rows: source_file_name (the same for every species, so it alone does not say whose dump it is), sha256, release, rows_read, every data row read and checked, in rows, and rows_kept, the rows whose two species are both snapshot species, in rows.

pairs is a data.frame, one row per species pair (a, b) with a sorting first, (s, s) included: species_a, species_b, and the relationships between them in rows - row_count, one row each, never merged or picked; ortholog_count, always 0 for (s, s); paralog_count, always 0 between two species; and homoeolog_count. See proteins_orthology_pair.

written is NULL without out. With it, a list: directory, absolute; manifest, the path of manifest.json, which lists every input and file with its sha256; and files, a data.frame of every file written but the manifest, in order of path: path (relative to directory, with forward slashes), rows (rows in the Parquet table, NA for views.sql, 0 for a pair with no relationship, which is still written), bytes (the file's size in bytes) and sha256.

pair_status is NULL without pair_status. With it, a list: from_species, to_species, row_count (every gene of from_species, in genes), status_counts (a named vector, status to genes with it, every status present in mzLib's order, zeros included), column_names, and records, a data.frame with one row per gene in order of gene id: gene_id, gene_name (NA when the GTF gives none: a label, never a key), gene_biotype and status. caveats names this call's traps.

What each status means

It says how far Compara's inference got, not what biology holds. has_ortholog: at least one ortholog in to_species. no_edge_in_shared_tree: the gene's tree holds a to_species gene, and Compara called no ortholog to it - the nearest the data comes to "no ortholog exists". tree_lacks_target_species: the gene's tree holds no to_species gene, so nothing was compared. not_in_any_tree: the gene is in the gene set but in no gene tree, so no call was attempted. Every biotype is a row, so choose your denominator by filtering on gene_biotype. One status's genes are ps$records$gene_id[ps$records$status == "not_in_any_tree"], with ps <- snap$pair_status.

The traps

The gene set and the dumps must be one release. A homology naming a gene its gene set lacks is refused as an mzlib_bridge_error (InvalidDataException): that is what a GTF and dumps from different releases look like. Use the primary-assembly GTF, as for proteins_resolve_genes. Keep Ensembl's file names: mzLib holds the gene trees and the dumps to release only when their names carry it, and a caveat says which were not checked. A directory that is not empty is refused as out: a snapshot is written once, and next release's goes in a new directory.

Wraps

Wire verb genes orthology. Generated from the bridge's verb spec genes.orthology.yaml (bridge commit 45833ca804d6) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

release

string; required; range an Ensembl release number, e.g. 116. The Ensembl release of the Compara inputs. Required, never defaulted: the release is part of the answer. mzLib holds the gene trees and every dump to it, but only when their file names carry a release (Compara.116.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz, vertebrates.GeneTree_content.default.e116.txt.gz); a renamed file is not checked, and the result's caveats say which. A GTF's own number is not compared with it: Ensembl publishes some species with their own annotation release (Saccharomyces_cerevisiae.R64-1-1.63.gtf.gz in release 116), so mzLib holds a gene set to the dumps by content instead.

wire --species

string[]; required; range >= 1 line; each exactly three tab-separated fields. Read from stdin (not an option), first: one line per species, the species' Ensembl production name (homo_sapiens, as the dumps' species column spells it), a tab, gtf or gene-set, a tab, and the path. gtf is an Ensembl primary-assembly GTF, plain or .gz, read with EnsemblGeneSet.LoadGtf; gene-set is the compact table mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter makes from one, read with EnsemblGeneSetReader.Load, which keeps the GTF's provenance. These lines are the snapshot's species. A species listed twice, a kind other than gtf or gene-set, or a missing file is a usage error. Blank lines are skipped. Not an argument here: rendered from gtfs and gene_sets, two named character vectors from Ensembl production name to path, one stdin line per species.

dumps

string[]; required; range exactly one per species. Read from stdin (not an option), after a line holding only –: one Compara homology dump path per line (homologies/SPECIES/Compara.RELEASE.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz, plain or .gz), each read with ComparaHomologyDump.Load for every species given. The dump's genome is read from its rows, not its name. mzLib requires EVERY species' dump: Compara puts each of a pair's relationships in one of the pair's two dumps, arbitrarily, so a missing dump would silently lose them. A missing dump, two of one species, or one of a species not given is mzLib's refusal, a usage error.

gene_trees (wire --gene-trees)

path; required. Compara's gene-tree membership dump, COLLECTION.GeneTree_content.default.eRELEASE.txt.gz (plain or .gz), read with ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load. It is what tells a gene whose tree holds no gene of the other species from one whose tree does but got no ortholog call.

restrict_gene_trees (wire --restrict-gene-trees)

flag; default FALSE. Keep only the gene-tree members in the given gene sets (ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load with restrictTo, the gene sets). Absent: mzLib's default, restrictTo null, which keeps every gene in the file, 4.2 million for the vertebrate collection of release 116 (mzLib's ComparaGeneTreeContent remarks). The snapshot, its id and every written byte are the same either way; only memory, gene_trees.member_count and gene_trees.restricted_to_gene_sets differ. mzLib checks the one-tree and one-canonical-protein rules only on the genes kept.

out

path; default absent; range a directory that does not exist or is empty. Write the snapshot to this directory with OrthologySnapshotWriter.WriteAsync: Parquet tables (zstd) genes/SPECIES.parquet, members/SPECIES.parquet and pairs/A__B.parquet, plus views.sql (DuckDB table macros) and manifest.json. The directory and its subfolders are created. A DIRECTORY, not a .tsv file: the PYB-1 extension rule is for options that write one table. mzLib refuses a directory that is not empty, because a snapshot is written once and compared with a later one, never updated in place; the bridge applies that same refusal, and refuses a path that is a file, before any input is read. Absent: nothing is written.

pair_status (wire --pair-status)

string; default absent; range FROM,TO: two different species of the snapshot. Return pair_status: every gene of FROM's gene set, in ordinal order of gene id, with its status in TO (OrthologySnapshot.PairStatus). Two production names separated by a comma, e.g. homo_sapiens,mus_musculus. Both must be species given on stdin, and different; the bridge checks that before any input is read, with the rule mzLib's PairStatus applies. One direction per call: status is not symmetric. Absent: pair_status is null.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

release

string; never NA. The --release given (OrthologySnapshot.Release).

species

string[]; never NA. The snapshot's species, Ensembl production names, in ordinal order (OrthologySnapshot.Species).

format

string; never NA. ensembl-orthology-snapshot (OrthologySnapshotWriter.FormatName): what manifest.json's format says.

format_version

int; never NA. 1 at d10017ce (OrthologySnapshotWriter.FormatVersion).

snapshot_id

string; never NA. OrthologySnapshotWriter.SnapshotId: lower-case hex sha256 over the format, the release, the species and every input's sha256. The same inputs give the same id, written or not; with --out it is manifest.json's snapshot_id. Record it with any result drawn from the snapshot.

identical_duplicates_dropped

int; in rows; never NA. Homology rows met in both of a pair's dumps, identical in every value, and counted once (OrthologySnapshot.IdenticalDuplicatesDropped). 0 in release 116, whose dumps partition; counted so a change is visible.

gene_sets

map<string,object>; never NA. Species to its gene set, in species order; each value has genes resolve's gene_set fields (typed under result.tables.gene_sets).

gene_trees

object; never NA. The gene-tree file and what was kept from it (typed under result.tables.gene_trees).

dumps

map<string,object>; never NA. Species (the dump's genome, read from its rows) to its homology dump, in species order (typed under result.tables.dumps).

pairs

object[]; never NA. One entry per species pair (a, b) with a <= b in ordinal order, (s, s) included, in OrthologySnapshot.Pairs order: how many relationships of each class it holds (typed under result.tables.pairs).

written

object; NA when no --out was given; nothing was written. The written snapshot: its directory and every file but manifest.json, which sits beside them (typed under result.tables.written).

pair_status

object; NA when no --pair-status was given. {from_species, to_species, row_count, status_counts, column_names, columns}: one row per gene of from_species (typed under result.tables.pair_status and result.tables.pair_status_columns).

caveats

string[]; never NA. This call's traps: an input whose file name carries no release (not checked against --release), dumps sharing one file name (source_dump cannot tell them apart), a GTF named for another release, identical duplicate rows, unrestricted gene trees holding genes outside the gene sets.

Fields of gene_sets

source_file_name

string; never NA. The GTF's file name; for a gene-set table, still the GTF's (EnsemblGeneSet.SourceFileName).

sha256

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the GTF's bytes as read, the compressed bytes for a .gz (EnsemblGeneSet.SourceSha256). manifest.json's gene_set_sha256 and genes resolve's gene_set_sha256 carry the same value, so a resolution and a snapshot can be checked against one gene set.

release

string; NA when the GTF's file name carries no release. The annotation release from the GTF's name; it may differ from --release (see the release param).

genome_build

string; NA when the GTF has no #!genome-build header. e.g. GRCh38.p14.

genebuild_last_updated

string; NA when the GTF has no #!genebuild-last-updated header. The header's value.

gene_count

int; in genes; never NA. Genes in the set, every biotype.

Fields of gene_trees

gene_trees$source_file_name (wire source_file_name)

string; never NA. The file's name.

gene_trees$sha256 (wire sha256)

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the file's bytes as read (compressed for a .gz).

gene_trees$release (wire release)

string; NA when the file name carries no .eRELEASE.txt suffix, so the release was not checked. The release parsed from the file name.

gene_trees$collection (wire collection)

string; NA when the file name does not start COLLECTION.GeneTree_content.. The Compara collection, e.g. vertebrates; manifest.json's collection.

gene_trees$member_count (wire member_count)

int; in genes; never NA. Genes held from the file (ComparaGeneTreeContent.Count): every gene in it, or with --restrict-gene-trees only those in the gene sets.

gene_trees$restricted_to_gene_sets (wire restricted_to_gene_sets)

string[]; NA when no --restrict-gene-trees: every gene in the file was kept. The sha256s of the gene sets the members were restricted to, in ordinal order (ComparaGeneTreeContent.RestrictedToGeneSets).

Fields of dumps

source_file_name

string; never NA. The dump's file name. Ensembl gives every species' dump the same name, so this alone does not say which dump it is: the key does.

sha256

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the file's bytes as read (compressed for a .gz).

release

string; NA when the file name does not start Compara.RELEASE., so the release was not checked. The release parsed from the file name.

rows_read

int; in rows; never NA. Every data row read and checked, kept or not (ComparaHomologyDump.RowsRead).

rows_kept

int; in rows; never NA. Rows whose two species are both snapshot species (ComparaHomologyDump.Rows). The rest name a species not given.

Fields of pairs

species_a

string; never NA. The species that sorts first; side A of every row in pairs/A__B.parquet.

species_b

string; never NA. The other species; the same as species_a for the paralogs of one species.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Relationships between the two (OrthologySnapshot.Pair), one row each, never merged or picked; the rows of pairs/A__B.parquet.

ortholog_count

int; in rows; never NA. Of those, ortholog_one2one, ortholog_one2many or ortholog_many2many (relationship_class ortholog). Always 0 for (s, s).

paralog_count

int; in rows; never NA. within_species_paralog, other_paralog or gene_split. Always 0 between two species.

homoeolog_count

int; in rows; never NA. homoeolog_one2one, homoeolog_one2many or homoeolog_many2many: between subgenomes of one polyploid species.

Fields of written

written$directory (wire directory)

string; never NA. The --out directory, absolute. manifest.json is in it.

written$files (wire files)

object[]; never NA. Every file written but manifest.json, in ordinal order of path (OrthologySnapshotWriter's SnapshotManifest.Files): {path, rows, bytes, sha256} (typed under result.tables.written_files).

Fields of written$files

a data.frame, one row per file written but manifest.json.

path

string; never NA. Relative to directory, with forward slashes, e.g. pairs/homo_sapiens__mus_musculus.parquet.

rows

int; in rows; NA when the file is not a table (views.sql). Rows in the Parquet table; 0 for a pair with no relationship, which is still written.

bytes

int; in bytes; never NA. The file's size.

sha256

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the file; manifest.json lists the same.

Fields of pair_status

pair_status$from_species (wire from_species)

string; never NA. FROM: whose genes the rows are.

pair_status$to_species (wire to_species)

string; never NA. TO: the species each status is about.

pair_status$row_count (wire row_count)

int; in genes; never NA. Every gene of from_species' gene set, all biotypes.

pair_status$status_counts (wire status_counts)

map<string,int>; in genes; never NA. Status name to genes with it, every OrthologyStatus in mzLib's order, zeros included. not_in_gene_set is always 0 here: every row is a gene of the gene set.

pair_status$column_names (wire column_names)

string[]; never NA. gene_id, gene_name, gene_biotype, status.

pair_status$records (wire columns)

table; never NA. Column name to one value per gene.

Fields of pair_status$records

a data.frame, one row per gene.

gene_id

string; never NA. Stable Ensembl gene id, unversioned as Ensembl GTFs write it.

gene_name

string; NA when the GTF gives the gene no gene_name (common for novel lncRNAs). The release's gene_name: a display label, never a key.

gene_biotype

string; never NA. The release's gene_biotype, unknown when the GTF omits it. Filter on it to choose the denominator: all biotypes are rows, and protein_coding alone is not the same set.

status

string; never NA. OrthologySnapshot.StatusName: has_ortholog (at least one ortholog in to_species), no_edge_in_shared_tree (the gene's tree holds a to_species gene and Compara called no ortholog to it: the closest the data comes to no ortholog exists), tree_lacks_target_species (the tree holds no to_species gene, so nothing was compared), or not_in_any_tree (in the gene set but in no gene tree: no call was attempted).

Fields of parquet_genes

the columns of genes/SPECIES.parquet in a written snapshot; mzLibR does not read Parquet.

gene_id

string; never NA. genes/SPECIES.parquet, one row per gene of the gene set.

gene_version

int; NA when the GTF gives no gene_version (absent is not 0). The gene_version attribute.

gene_biotype

string; never NA. unknown when the GTF omits it.

gene_name

string; NA when the GTF gives no gene_name. A display label.

seq_region

string; never NA. The GTF's first column: chromosome or scaffold.

species

string; never NA. The production name.

Fields of parquet_members

the columns of members/SPECIES.parquet in a written snapshot.

gene_id

string; never NA. members/SPECIES.parquet, one row per gene of the gene set that is in a gene tree.

species

string; never NA. The production name.

group_id

string; never NA. compara-RELEASE:TREE_ID, so a tree id is never compared across releases.

source_group_id

string; never NA. Compara's gene-tree stable id, e.g. ENSGT00940000153582.

canonical_protein_id

string; never NA. The protein Compara used for the gene (the row flagged Y).

Fields of parquet_pairs

the columns of pairs/A__B.parquet in a written snapshot.

homology_id

string; never NA. pairs/A__B.parquet, one row per relationship, ordered by homology id. Compara's id, unique within a release.

relationship_type

string; never NA. Compara's homology_type verbatim, e.g. ortholog_one2many.

relationship_class

string; never NA. ortholog, paralog or homoeolog (ComparaHomologyDump.ClassName).

species_a

string; never NA. The species that sorts first.

species_b

string; never NA. The other species.

gene_a

string; never NA. Side A's gene; every value moves with its gene when a row is reoriented.

protein_a

string; never NA. Side A's protein in the alignment.

identity_a

float; in percent; NA when Compara gave NULL. Percentage of A's protein identical to B's in the alignment, 0 to 100.

gene_b

string; never NA. Side B's gene.

protein_b

string; never NA. Side B's protein.

identity_b

float; in percent; NA when Compara gave NULL. Percentage of B's protein identical to A's, 0 to 100. Not identity_a: each is over its own protein's length.

dn

float; in nonsynonymous substitutions per nonsynonymous site; NA when Compara gave NULL (it computes dN for few comparisons). Compara's dn verbatim.

ds

float; in synonymous substitutions per synonymous site; NA when Compara gave NULL. Compara's ds verbatim.

goc_score

int; in score, 0 to 100; NA when Compara gave NULL (not computed for this pair). Gene order conservation score.

wga_coverage

float; in percent; NA when Compara gave NULL (no whole-genome alignment for this pair). Whole-genome alignment coverage, 0 to 100.

is_high_confidence

bool; NA when Compara gave NULL: it declines to say, which is not false. Compara's high-confidence flag.

source_dump

string; never NA. The FILE NAME of the dump the row was read from. Which of a pair's two dumps holds a row is arbitrary, so this is provenance, not meaning; and as Ensembl names every dump the same, it cannot say which species' dump.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--release or --gene-trees missing or given without a value; --out or --pair-status given without a value; a value after --restrict-gene-trees

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

no species lines on stdin, no line holding only –, or no dump paths after it; a species line that is not species, tab, gtf or gene-set, tab, path; a species listed twice

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

a GTF, gene-set table, dump or gene-trees file that does not exist; --out naming a file or a directory that is not empty (OrthologySnapshotWriter.WriteAsync's refusal, applied before any input is read)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--pair-status not two comma-separated names, naming a species not given on stdin, or one species twice (the rule of OrthologySnapshot.PairStatus, applied before any input is read)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib's OrthologySnapshot.Build refused the inputs as not fitting together (ArgumentException, with mzLib's message): the gene trees or a dump name a release other than --release; a dump is of a species not given, two dumps are of one species, or a species has no dump

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

a file mzLib's reader refuses (InvalidDataException, naming file and line): a GTF gene row without gene_id; a table that is not a gene-set table; a dump with other columns, a short row, a value that is not a number, an unknown homology_type, a paralog between two species, an ortholog within one, or a second genome; a gene-tree row without four cells or with a flag other than Y or N, or a kept gene in two trees or without exactly one canonical protein

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

OrthologySnapshot.Build found data that breaks the snapshot's rules (InvalidDataException): one gene in two species' gene sets, a homology naming a gene its species' gene set lacks (the gene set and the dumps are from different releases), or one homology id with two different rows

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

the snapshot could not be written (IOException from the disk)

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Every species' homology dump is required, and mzLib refuses a call without one. Compara's README warns that each genome's dump holds an arbitrary subset of its relationships, and in practice they partition: in release 116 every human-mouse orthology is in the mouse dump and none is in the human one, so the dump named after one species gives a complete-looking, badly incomplete answer.

  • Orthology is asserted per species pair and is not transitive: A~B and B~C do not make A~C. Never chain pairs into groups. The written views.sql's species_set3 macro, and mzLib's OrthologySnapshot.SpeciesSet, form a tuple only when every two members are orthologs.

  • Nothing is picked, merged or collapsed: a one-to-many or many-to-many orthology is several rows, and a gene's paralogs are the pair (s, s).

  • A status says how far Compara's inference got, not what biology holds. no_edge_in_shared_tree is the nearest the data comes to no ortholog exists; tree_lacks_target_species and not_in_any_tree mean nothing was compared.

  • Every biotype is in pair_status and in genes/SPECIES.parquet. Which genes form a denominator is the caller's choice: filter on gene_biotype. mzLib's own human-to-mouse check counted protein-coding plus IG and TR genes, which is not the same set as protein_coding alone.

  • Values are Compara's, verbatim: a NULL in a dump stays null in the Parquet (identity, dn, ds, goc_score, wga_coverage, is_high_confidence), never 0 or false. identity_a and identity_b differ because each is over its own protein.

  • The gene set and the dumps must be from one release: mzLib refuses a homology whose gene is not in its species' gene set. Use the primary-assembly GTF (Species.Assembly.Release.gtf.gz), as for genes resolve.

  • A snapshot is written once. The same inputs give the same bytes and the same snapshot_id, so a later release is a new directory compared with the old one; a directory that is not empty is refused, never overwritten.

  • mzLib ships a writer and no reader. Query the Parquet with DuckDB (load views.sql for the orthologs, pair_status and species_set3 macros), pyarrow, polars or R's arrow.

  • Ensembl names every species' dump Compara.RELEASE.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz in its own folder, and the pairs tables' source_dump column records only the file name, so it cannot tell two species' dumps apart. manifest.json's inputs list each dump with its species and sha256.

Performance

Everything is read into memory, and the inputs are large: human release 116's GTF is 141 MB compressed (mzLib's EnsemblGeneSet remarks), and the vertebrate gene-tree file holds 4.2 million genes unless --restrict-gene-trees keeps only the given species'. For human, mouse and rat at release 116, mzLib #1381 reports the build from the three dumps at about 20 s and the written snapshot (13 files, 9.0 MB) at about 40 s more. No call here takes a degree of parallelism, so there is no --threads. Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.proteins.build_orthology

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::proteins::build_orthology_with with OrthologyOptions

  • R (mzLibR): proteins_build_orthology

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • result.tables (gene_sets, gene_trees, dumps, pairs, written, pair_status and the Parquet tables) is not validated by tools/check_verbs.py, which checks only envelope_fields, columns and bulk. Bridge tests pin each nested object's keys (GenesOrthologyTests).

  • The Parquet tables' units are mzLib's doc comments (ComparaHomology: identity percent, goc_score and wga_coverage 0 to 100). dn and ds are written as dN and dS conventionally are, substitutions per site; neither mzLib nor this bridge has checked Compara's own definition.

  • Only one pair-status direction per call, and no SpeciesSet tuples or ortholog rows on the wire: the written Parquet and views.sql answer those. Whether a binding needs them without a Parquet reader (pyMzLib has no third-party dependency) is open.

  • source_dump records the dump's file name, which Ensembl gives every species' dump (PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: mzLib could record the dump's genome, or the path under homologies/, beside it).

  • Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.

References

  • doi:10.1101/gr.073585.107: Ensembl Compara gene trees, the duplication-aware phylogenies its orthology and paralogy calls are read from (Vilella et al. 2009, Genome Res 19:327)

  • doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1239: Ensembl releases, their GTFs and the Compara homology dumps (Ensembl 2026, NAR)

See also

proteins_orthology_pair, proteins_resolve_genes

Examples


# mzLib's own test world: four human genes, three mouse and two rat, with every human-mouse
# row in the mouse dump, as in release 116.
gtfs <- c(homo_sapiens = "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf",
          mus_musculus = "Mus_musculus.GRCm39.116.gtf",
          rattus_norvegicus = "Rattus_norvegicus.GRCr8.116.gtf")
dumps <- paste0("homologies/", names(gtfs), "/Compara.116.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz")
snap <- proteins_build_orthology("116", gtfs = gtfs, dumps = dumps,
  gene_trees = "vertebrates.GeneTree_content.default.e116.txt.gz",
  pair_status = c("homo_sapiens", "mus_musculus"))
snap
#> <mzlibr_orthology_snapshot> Ensembl 116, 3 species: homo_sapiens, mus_musculus, rattus_norvegicus
#>   snapshot_id 5487ebcabe48... (record it with any result)
#>   orthologs: homo_sapiens~mus_musculus 3, homo_sapiens~rattus_norvegicus 1, mus_musculus~rattus_norvegicus 2
#>   homo_sapiens in mus_musculus: has_ortholog 2, tree_lacks_target_species 1, not_in_any_tree 1
#>   ! The dumps of homo_sapiens, mus_musculus, rattus_norvegicus share the file name Compara.116.protein_default.homologies.tsv.gz, and the pairs tables' source_dump column holds only the file name, so it cannot say which species' dump a row came from. manifest.json's inputs list each dump with its species and sha256.
#>   ! The gene trees were read unrestricted: 9 genes were held in memory, 8 of them in the given gene sets. --restrict-gene-trees holds only those and gives the same snapshot.
snap$pair_status$records[, c("gene_id", "gene_biotype", "status")]
#>           gene_id   gene_biotype                    status
#> 1 ENSG00000000001 protein_coding              has_ortholog
#> 2 ENSG00000000002 protein_coding              has_ortholog
#> 3 ENSG00000000003 protein_coding tree_lacks_target_species
#> 4 ENSG00000000004 protein_coding           not_in_any_tree
snap$dumps[, c("species", "rows_kept")]
#>             species rows_kept
#> 1      homo_sapiens         1
#> 2      mus_musculus         5
#> 3 rattus_norvegicus         1
proteins_orthology_pair(snap, "mus_musculus", "homo_sapiens")$row_count
#> [1] 3

# With out = the snapshot is written, and its id is the same:
written <- proteins_build_orthology("116", gtfs = gtfs, dumps = dumps,
  gene_trees = "vertebrates.GeneTree_content.default.e116.txt.gz",
  restrict_gene_trees = TRUE, out = "compara-116")
identical(written$snapshot_id, snap$snapshot_id)
#> [1] TRUE
head(written$written$files[, c("path", "rows")], 7)
#>                                       path rows
#> 1               genes/homo_sapiens.parquet    4
#> 2               genes/mus_musculus.parquet    3
#> 3          genes/rattus_norvegicus.parquet    2
#> 4             members/homo_sapiens.parquet    3
#> 5             members/mus_musculus.parquet    3
#> 6        members/rattus_norvegicus.parquet    2
#> 7 pairs/homo_sapiens__homo_sapiens.parquet    0
